sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is an incomplete skeleton containing limb elements, the synsacrum, pelvis, pectoral girdle, and vertebrae.
This fossil possesses a relatively long spur compared to its body size, a trait suggesting it was a male.
Fossils of Eopavo were discovered in China within the Liushu Formation.
Specifically, Eopavo hezhengensis was found in late Miocene deposits in the Linxia Basin, near the edge of the Tibetan Plateau.
Researchers suggest that Eopavo's small body size was likely an adaptation to this high-elevation environment.
The long spur implies the animal may have engaged in aggressive physical contact between males, similar to some modern relatives.
The only known species in the genus Eopavo is Eopavo hezhengensis.
Eopavo is classified within the clade Pavonini, which includes the living genera Pavo and Afropavo.
This animal lived during the Miocene epoch, specifically the Late Miocene.
It inhabited a high-elevation savanna habitat, which contrasts with the humid forests preferred by modern peafowl.

While Yu et al. (2026) suggested the peafowl clade likely originated on the Tibetan Plateau, the disjunct distribution of modern peafowl in southern Asia and central Africa has led to ongoing debates about the clade's origin and evolution.
